Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
The churn model `churn-hgb-v3` scored an offline validation AUC of 0.805, but 0.656 in its first live month
(`/app/INCIDENT.md`). Its feature pipeline in `/app/churn` already uses only events stamped before each prediction
(`/app/CHANGELOG.md`), yet the live scoring service computed other values for the same predictions. The live service
computes every feature at the moment of a prediction from the warehouse tables as they stand at that moment
(`/app/live/features.py`). The pipeline builds its training table from an extract taken later (`/app/data`, this
brand's warehouse at 2026-03-05T00:00:00Z). The tables are described in `/app/docs/WAREHOUSE.md`, the warehouse's own
records of its job runs and transactions are in `/app/data/_ops/`, and samples of what the live service computed are
in `/app/logs/`.

Fix `python -m churn.build_features --data <dir> --out <file.parquet>` (run from `/app`) so that, for every row of the
extract's `scoring_points.csv`, each feature is the value the live service would have computed for that customer at
that row's `as_of`, had it been running then against the warehouse as it stood at that moment (exactly the rows and
values committed to it before that moment, in the tables its queries name). This must hold for any extract with the
layout of `/app/data`. Keep every feature of `/app/live/features.py` whose live value the extract determines for every
row; leave out any feature whose live value the extract cannot determine for some rows.

How the result is checked:
- `python3 -m churn.build_features --data <dir> --out <file.parquet>` is run from a copy of `/app` at another path, as
  an unprivileged user, on extracts of the company's other brands: the same seven CSV files, `_ops/` folder and layout
  as `/app/data`, about the same size and period, with other customers, events and load histories (their own job runs,
  failures and migrations). It must exit with status 0 and write the parquet file. Do not rely on network access, on
  absolute paths into `/app`, or on anything in `/app/data` or `/app/logs`.
- The output must have exactly one row per row of the extract's `scoring_points.csv`, with the columns `customer_id`,
  `as_of` and every kept feature, named as in `/app/live/features.py`. Extra columns, row order and column order do not
  matter, but a column named after a feature that should be left out fails unless all its values are null.
  `customer_id` may be any integer type; `as_of` a timestamp (time-zone aware, or naive meaning UTC) or an ISO 8601
  string; the integer features (`orders_7d`, `orders_30d`, `spend_30d_cents`, `tickets_30d`) any numeric type holding
  whole numbers; a null a parquet null or NaN.
- Every value must equal what the live service would have computed: integer features exactly, other numbers within
  1e-6 plus 1e-9 times the expected value, strings exactly, nulls exactly where the live service would have had no value.
- An extract is also changed in everything the warehouse did not yet hold at some cut time (in any table, whatever the
  date of the event a row records) and the command is run again: every prediction with `as_of` at or before the cut
  must keep the same feature values (within the tolerances above). The changed extract is still a copy of the
  warehouse at the same moment as the original extract, in the same layout; only what the warehouse did not yet hold
  at the cut differs, and its `_ops/` records match it: every record dated before the cut is unchanged, and the later
  records describe the changed extract.
- Each run is stopped after 60 seconds and then fails. The grading container has the same resources as this one
  (2 vCPUs, 4 GiB), and `/app/data` is about the size of the graded extracts, so time a run on it. Graded runs set
  `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`.
- `python -m churn.train` is not graded; it may help to check the work.

Only /app is kept when we grade: folders named `data`, `__pycache__` or `.venv` anywhere under /app are dropped, and the packages already installed are available.

# INC-2077: churn-hgb-v3 scores far worse live than in validation

Status: open. Owner: ML platform on-call. Opened 2026-03-04, updated 2026-03-05.

## What happened
- `churn-hgb-v3` is trained on the feature table that the offline pipeline builds (`churn/`, v3 in `CHANGELOG.md`).
  Built from this brand's extract (`data/`, the warehouse at 2026-03-05T00:00:00Z), that table gives
  **offline validation AUC 0.805** in `python -m churn.train` (trained on the predictions before 2025-09-01,
  validated on those of 2025-09-01 to 2025-11-30).
- The model went live on 2026-01-01. The live scoring service computes the features of each request itself, from the
  warehouse at the moment of the request (`live/features.py`). On the 3,415 predictions of January 2026, whose 30-day
  outcomes have all landed in `labels`: **live AUC 0.656**.
- The model and its hyperparameters did not change between validation and launch.

## Tried so far
- Retrained with much stronger regularization and shallower trees (`--l2 50 --max-depth 2`): offline AUC 0.813. The
  offline number did not fall, so this is not ordinary overfitting.
- Compared the live service with `live/features.py` by hand on 200 January requests: the service computes exactly what
  its queries say.
- Pulled a random sample of about 10% of the requests of January 2026, with the values the service computed:
  `logs/live_2026-01_sample.jsonl`, 365 requests, one JSON object per line with `customer_id`, `as_of`, `trigger`, the
  11 `features` and the model's `score`.

## Next step (model team)
`churn-hgb-v4` is to be trained on a feature table that matches what the live service computed for every past
prediction. Every feature whose live value can be matched for every prediction is kept; any feature whose live value
cannot be matched is dropped from v4.

# Changelog: the offline feature pipeline (`churn/`)

## v3 (2025-12-19): the training table of churn-hgb-v3
Fixes INC-2041: in four places, v2 used events stamped at or after the prediction time `t`.
- `windows.py`: the order, spend and ticket windows are `[t - W days, t)` on the exact event timestamps. v2 summed
  whole UTC days, the day of `t` included, so events later on the prediction day were counted.
- `status.py`: the latest snapshot dated before `date(t)`. A snapshot dated D records the status at the end of day D;
  v2 took the customer's latest snapshot in the extract, which is often dated after `t`.
- `impute.py`: a missing `app_minutes_7d` takes the customer's most recent earlier reading only. v2 filled backward
  first, from a later reading.
- `encoding.py`: `te_district` counts only labels whose 30-day window had closed before `t` (`as_of + 30 days < t`),
  for the district and for the prior alike. v2 used every label in the extract, the prediction's own and later ones
  included.

Also in v3:
- `attributes.py` (new): `plan` and `days_since_last_login` from the customer record, the two features of the live
  service that v2 did not build. A last login at or after `t` is ignored (the feature is null then).
- `extract.py` loads the seven tables described in `docs/WAREHOUSE.md`.
- `train.py`: every column of the feature table other than `customer_id` and `as_of` is a model input, and string
  columns are one-hot encoded (v2 encoded `status` only); a column that holds no value at all is skipped.

- A query that starts at a moment t sees exactly the rows and values committed before t: a row committed at or after
  t is not seen, and a value overwritten at or after t is seen as it was before the overwrite, whatever the date of
  the event the row records.
- A query reads each table by the name it has when the query starts.
- `_loaded_at` is the commit time of the load that wrote the row; in `orders`, `_load_job` names that load.
- An extract is a copy of every table as the warehouse held it at one moment: the rows and values committed before

- Timestamps are UTC, written as ISO 8601 with a `Z` suffix and whole seconds (`2025-02-04T06:00:00Z`);
  `snapshot_date` is a UTC date (`YYYY-MM-DD`); amounts are integer cents. Columns whose names start with `_` are
  written by the loaders, not by the source systems.

## The scheduler's records (`_ops/`)
- `_ops/scheduler.log` has one UTC event per line, `<time> <job> run=<run> <event>`: each task's start
  (`state=running`) and end (`state=success` or `state=failed`), and between them the lines the task writes, such as
  the rows it selected or copied, the transaction it sent (`sent txn <n> to commit`), the statements it ran and the
  checks it made.

  statements).
- `_ops/commits.jsonl` is the commit log of the scheduled jobs: a transaction is committed if and only if its outcome
  is `commit`, and it is committed at its `at`; the scheduler's task states describe tasks, not commits.
- Change data capture (`tickets`), the sign-up service and the scoring service write without the scheduler and are not
  in `_ops/`.

## Tables

### `customers`
`customer_id, signup_at, plan, postcode_district, last_login_at, _updated_at`: one row per customer.
- The sign-up service writes the row at `signup_at`: the plan chosen at sign-up (`basic`, `plus` or `family`), the
  postcode district, an empty `last_login_at`, and `_updated_at` = `signup_at`. `signup_at` and `postcode_district`
  never change.
- `crm_sync` reads the CRM at its start. For each customer whose plan or last login in the CRM (the latest login to
  the app or website before the sync's start) differs from the row, it overwrites `plan` and `last_login_at` with the
  CRM's values and sets `_updated_at` to the sync's commit time.
- Only plan changes are logged (`plan_changes`); no history of `last_login_at` is kept.

### `plan_changes`
`customer_id, changed_at, old_plan, new_plan, _loaded_at`: one row per plan change that `crm_sync` has applied. Each
sync writes one row for every change made in the CRM before its start that no earlier sync applied; `changed_at` is
when the customer made the change in the CRM, `_loaded_at` the commit of the sync that applied it. A customer's rows
are every change applied since sign-up, so the earliest row's `old_plan` is the plan chosen at sign-up. When one sync
applies several changes of a customer, the plan after that sync is the `new_plan` of the latest of them (by

customer's billing weekday) or `ticket` (a request the support desk sends when a ticket is opened, for some of the
tickets, at the ticket's `opened_at`). `app_minutes_7d` is the product-analytics reading that came with the request (the customer's minutes in
the app over the last 7 days), empty when the request came without one (analytics export outages, devices offline).
`(customer_id, as_of)` is unique.

`order_id, customer_id, ordered_at, kind, amount_cents, _load_job, _loaded_at`. `kind` is `box` (the weekly box,
charged by billing at 05:30 on the customer's billing weekday; `ordered_at` is the charge) or `addon` (an extra item,
ordered at any time). Each order exists in the order system, which t

"""Build the churn feature table: python -m churn.build_features --data <dir> --out <file.parquet>"""
import argparse
import os

from churn.attributes import days_since_last_login, plan
from churn.encoding import district_encoding
from churn.extract import load_extract
from churn.impute import fill_app_minutes
from churn.status import latest_status
from churn.windows import activity_features, tenure_days

FEATURE_COLUMNS = ["orders_7d", "orders_30d", "spend_30d_cents", "tickets_30d", "days_since_last_order",
                   "tenure_days", "status", "plan", "days_since_last_login", "app_minutes_7d", "te_district"]


def build(data_dir):
    t = load_extract(data_dir)
    points = t["scoring_points"].reset_index(drop=True)
    feats = activity_features(points, t["orders"], t["tickets"])
    feats["tenure_days"] = tenure_days(points, t["customers"])
    feats["status"] = latest_status(points, t["status_snapshots"])
    feats["plan"] = plan(points, t["customers"])
    feats["days_since_last_login"] = days_since_last_login(points, t["customers"])
    feats["app_minutes_7d"] = fill_app_minutes(points)
    feats["te_district"] = district_encoding(points, t["labels"], t["customers"])
    return feats[["customer_id", "as_of"] + FEATURE_COLUMNS]


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--data", required=True, help="folder with the extract CSVs")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output parquet file")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    feats = build(a.data)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(a.out)), exist_ok=True)
    feats.to_parquet(a.out, index=False)
    print(f"wrote {len(feats)} rows x {feats.shape[1]} columns to {a.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    return ((ts - EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)).to_numpy(dtype="int64")


def district_encoding(points, labels, customers, m=PRIOR_WEIGHT):

    pt_d = points["customer_id"].map(district)
    codes, _ = pd.factorize(pd.concat([lab_d, pt_d], ignore_index=True))
    lab_code, pt_code = codes[:len(labels)].astype("int64"), codes[len(labels):].astype("int64")
    closed = _seconds(labels["as_of"]) + LABEL_WINDOW_DAYS * 86400
    y = labels["churned_30d"].to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    t = _seconds(points["as_of"])

    order = np.argsort(closed, kind="stable")
    ycum = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(y[order])])
    N = np.searchsorted(closed[order], t, side="left")
    S = ycum[N]
    prior = np.full(len(t), DEFAULT_PRIOR)
    has = N > 0
    prior[has] = S[has] / N[has]

    key = lab_code * STRIDE + closed
    o2 = np.argsort(key, kind="stable")
    ycum2 = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(y[o2])])
    hi = np.searchsorted(key[o2], pt_code * STRIDE + t, side="left")
    lo = np.searchsorted(key[o2], pt_code * STRIDE, side="left")
    n, s = hi - lo, ycum2[hi] - ycum2[lo]
    return pd.Series((s + m * prior) / (n + m), index=points.index, dtype="float64")

"""Train and validate the churn model: python -m churn.train --features <file.parquet> --data <dir> [--l2 1.0]

Time-based split: train on predictions before 2025-09-01, validate on 2025-09-01 .. 2025-11-30. Every column of the
feature table other than customer_id and as_of is a model input: numeric columns as they are (a null is a missing
value), string columns one-hot encoded. A column that holds no value at all is skipped.
"""
import argparse
import os

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score

KEYS = ["customer_id", "as_of"]
LABEL = "churned_30d"
TRAIN_END = pd.Timestamp("2025-09-01", tz="UTC")
VALID_END = pd.Timestamp("2025-12-01", tz="UTC")


def inputs(feats):
    return [c for c in feats.columns if c not in KEYS and c != LABEL]


def categories(feats):
    """Sorted values of each string column (one indicator column per value)."""
    return {c: sorted(feats[c].dropna().astype(str).unique()) for c in inputs(feats)
            if not pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(feats[c])}


def design_matrix(feats, cats):
    X = feats[[c for c in inputs(feats) if c not in cats]].astype("float64").copy()
    for c, values in cats.items():
        for v in values:
            X[f"{c}_{v}"] = (feats[c] == v).astype("float64")
    return X


def make_model(l2=1.0, max_depth=4):
    return HistGradientBoostingClassifier(max_iter=300, learning_rate=0.05, max_depth=max_depth,
                                          l2_regularization=l2, early_stopping=False, random_state=0)


def train_validate(feats, labels, l2=1.0, max_depth=4):
    """Fit on labelled predictions before TRAIN_END, validate on TRAIN_END .. VALID_END."""
    df = feats.merge(labels[KEYS + [LABEL]], on=KEYS, how="inner").dropna(axis=1, how="all")  # no value: no input
    cats = categories(df)
    tr = df[df["as_of"] < TRAIN_END]
    va = df[(df["as_of"] >= TRAIN_END) & (df["as_of"] < VALID_END)]
    model = make_model(l2, max_depth).fit(design_matrix(tr, cats), tr[LABEL])
    auc = roc_auc_score(va[LABEL], model.predict_proba(design_matrix(va, cats))[:, 1])
    return model, cats, auc, tr, va


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--features", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--data", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--l2", type=float, default=1.0, help="L2 regularization")
    ap.add_argument("--max-depth", type=int, default=4)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    feats = pd.read_parquet(a.features)
    feats["as_of"] = pd.to_datetime(feats["as_of"], utc=True)
    labels = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(a.data, "labels.csv"))
    labels["as_of"] = pd.to_datetime(labels["as_of"], utc=True)
    model, cats, auc, tr, va = train_validate(feats, labels, a.l2, a.max_depth)
    print(f"train rows {len(tr)}, validation rows {len(va)}, validation churn rate {va['churned_30d'].mean():.3f}")
    print(f"offline validation AUC: {auc:.3f}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Activity features over trailing windows (orders, spend, tickets) and simple time-since features.

Point in time (INC-2041): a window is [t - W days, t) on the exact event timestamps, so an event stamped at or after
the prediction time is never counted and nothing later in the day leaks in.
"""
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

EPOCH = pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01", tz="UTC")
STRIDE = 10 ** 10  # composite key customer_id * STRIDE + epoch seconds (seconds stay below 1e10 until 2286)


def _seconds(ts):
    return ((ts - EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)).to_numpy(dtype="int64")


def _window(points, events, ts_col, days, amount_col=None):
    """Per prediction: number (and amount sum) of the customer's events with t - days <= ts < t."""
    ev_key = events["customer_id"].to_numpy(dtype="int64") * STRIDE + _seconds(events[ts_col])
    order = np.argsort(ev_key, kind="stable")
    ev_key = ev_key[order]
    cid = points["customer_id"].to_numpy(dtype="int64") * STRIDE
    t = _seconds(points["as_of"])
    hi = np.searchsorted(ev_key, cid + t, side="left")
    lo = np.searchsorted(ev_key, cid + t - days * 86400, side="left")
    count = hi - lo
    if amount_col is None:
        return count, None
    pref = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(events[amount_col].to_numpy(dtype="int64")[order])])
    return count, pref[hi] - pref[lo]


def activity_features(points, orders, tickets):
    out = points[["customer_id", "as_of"]].copy()
    out["orders_7d"], _ = _window(points, orders, "ordered_at", 7)
    out["orders_30d"], out["spend_30d_cents"] = _window(points, orders, "ordered_at", 30, "amount_cents")
    out["tickets_30d"], _ = _window(points, tickets, "opened_at", 30)

    # time since the last order strictly before the prediction
    o = orders.sort_values("ordered_at")[["customer_id", "ordered_at"]]
    left = out[["customer_id", "as_of"]].reset_index().sort_values("as_of")
    last = pd.merge_asof(left, o, left_on="as_of", right_on="ordered_at", by="customer_id",
                         allow_exact_matches=False).set_index("index").sort_index()["ordered_at"]
    out["days_since_last_order"] = (out["as_of"] - last).dt.total_seconds() / 86400
    return out


def tenure_days(points, customers):
    signup = points["customer_id"].map(customers.set_index("customer_id")["signup_at"])
    return (points["as_of"] - signup).dt.total_seconds() / 86400

Analysis: I now have a clear picture. The 11 live features and how they should be reconstructed point-in-time:
- orders_7d/orders_30d/spend_30d_cents/days_since_last_order: from orders, but an order is only visible at t if _loaded_at < t (plus the query's ordered_at window). Current code ignores _loaded_at.
- tickets_30d: tickets visible iff _loaded_at < t.
- status: live query takes max snapshot_date among _loaded_at < t (NO date(t) filter in the live SQL).
- tenure_days: (t - signup_at)/86400 (signup_at immutable).
- plan: mutable via crm_sync; reconstruct from plan_changes (_loaded_at < t) + signup plan.
- app_minutes_7d: row's own value else latest earlier (as_of < t) non-null scoring point.
- te_district: live uses ALL labels committed before t (filter _loaded_at < t), NOT as_of+30d < t.
- days_since_last_login: last_login_at has NO history -> NOT determinable -> DROP.

The best ground-truth validation is logs/live_2026-01_sample.jsonl (365 rows with live-computed features). I'll validate my reconstruction against it.

steps.reasoning_content:
Let me think about what's needed. I need to understand the data fully before writing the solution. Let me analyze the key challenge.

The task: For every row of scoring_points.csv, compute each feature as the live service would have computed at that row's `as_of`, against the warehouse as it stood at that moment (rows/values committed before that moment).

The live service queries run at `:now` = as_of. A query at time t sees exactly rows committed before t, and values overwritten at or after t are seen as they were before the overwrite.

So I need to reconstruct, for each prediction at time t, what the warehouse looked like at time t.

Let me go feature by feature.

**orders_7d, orders_30d, spend_30d_cents, days_since_last_order** — from `orders` table. Each order row has `_loaded_at` (commit time). An order is visible at time t iff `_loaded_at < t` (committed before t). The order is only in the table from its _loaded_at on. The query filters on `ordered_at` in [t-7d, t). So an order counts iff `_loaded_at < t` AND `ordered_at >= t - 7d` AND `ordered_at < t`.

Wait, but there's a subtlety: the query `WHERE ordered_at < :now`. So `ordered_at < t`. And `_loaded_at < t` for the row to exist. So both conditions.

Actually wait — can an order have `ordered_at` in the future relative to `t` but `_loaded_at < t`? The legacy_orders job selects orders from the order system where `ordered_at` in [day, day+1) and commits. So an order with ordered_at on day D is loaded on D+1 or so. So ordered_at is always in the past relative to _loaded_at. But could ordered_at be after some prediction's t even though _loaded_at < t? Yes. E.g., order with ordered_at = 2025-05-10, _loaded_at = 2025-05-11. A prediction at t=2025-05-11T12:00 sees this order (committed at 05-11 04:12 < 12:00), but ordered_at (05-10) < t so it counts in window if within range. Fine.

But could ordered_at > t with _loaded_at < t? That would require the order system to have an order with ordered_at in the future. The docs say orders exist from ordered_at on. Legacy job loads day by day. It's hard to imagine ordered_at > _loaded_at. But to be safe and correct, I should filter BOTH `_loaded_at < t` AND the query's `ordered_at` conditions. The correct simulation is: the row exists at time t iff committed before t (_loaded_at < t). Then apply the query's WHERE on ordered_at. So orders_7d counts orders where _loaded_at < t AND ordered_at >= t-7d AND ordered_at < t.

Actually the existing `_window` function in windows.py already does `ordered_at in [t-W, t)` via searchsorted on (customer_id, ordered_at). It does NOT filter on _loaded_at. I need to add `_loaded_at < t` filter. So an order only contributes if both committed before t and ordered_at in window.

Hmm, but wait — is it possible that an order with ordered_at < t but _loaded_at >= t? Yes! That's the key issue. An order placed (ordered_at) but not yet loaded into warehouse. """Gap filling for upstream readings that arrive with holes (analytics export outages, devices offline).

Point in time (INC-2041): a missing reading takes the customer's most recent earlier reading, never a later one; with
no earlier reading it stays null.
"""


def fill_app_minutes(points):
    """Fill missing app_minutes_7d from the same customer's last earlier reading."""
    pts = points.sort_values(["customer_id", "as_of"], kind="mergesort")
    filled = pts.groupby("customer_id")["app_minutes_7d"].ffill()
    return filled.reindex(points.index)
=====ATTR=====
"""Customer attributes from the customer record (new in v3): the subscription plan and the days since the last login.

Point in time: a last login at or after the prediction time is ignored (the feature is null then), so the feature
never looks ahead of t.
"""


def plan(points, customers):
    """The customer's subscription plan."""
    return points["customer_id"].map(customers.set_index("customer_id")["plan"])


def days_since_last_login(points, customers):
    """t minus the customer's last login, in days; null when the record has no login before t."""
    last = points["customer_id"].map(customers.set_index("customer_id")["last_login_at"])
    days = (points["as_of"] - last).dt.total_seconds() / 86400
    return days.where(last < points["as_of"])
=====STATUS=====
"""Account status from the billing system's status snapshots, point in time (INC-2041).

A snapshot dated D records the status at the end of day D, so a prediction at t may only use snapshots dated before
date(t).
"""
import pandas as pd


def latest_status(points, snapshots):
    """Status of the customer's latest snapshot dated before the prediction's UTC date (null if none)."""
    left = points[["customer_id"]].assign(day=points["as_of"].dt.floor("D")).reset_index()
    left = left.sort_values("day", kind="mergesort")
    snaps = snapshots.sort_values("snapshot_date", kind="mergesort")[["customer_id", "snapshot_date", "status"]]
    snaps = snaps.assign(snapshot_date=snaps["snapshot_date"].astype(left["day"].dtype))
    m = pd.merge_asof(left, snaps, left_on="day", right_on="snapshot_date", by="customer_id",
                      allow_exact_matches=False)
    return m.set_index("index")["status"].reindex(points.index)

"""Build the churn feature table: python -m churn.build_features --data <dir> --out <file.parquet>

For every row of scoring_points.csv, compute the value the live scoring service
(live/features.py) would have produced at that row's as_of against the warehouse
as it stood at that moment: only rows/values committed before as_of.

no history of the customer's last login) are left out.

import argparse
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from churn.extract import load_extract

EPOCH = pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01", tz="UTC")
STRIDE = 10 ** 10
DAY = 86400


def _sec(ts):
    return ((ts - EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)).to_numpy(dtype="int64")


def _te_district(points, labels, customers):
    """Live te_district: over all labels committed before t (loaded_at < t)."""
    district = customers.set_index("customer_id")["postcode_district"]
    lab = labels.copy()
    lab["_d"] = lab["customer_id"].map(district)
    lab = lab.dropna(subset=["_d"])
    pt_d = points["customer_id"].map(district)
    codes, _ = pd.factorize(pd.concat([lab["_d"], pt_d], ignore_index=True))
    lab_code = codes[: len(lab)].astype("int64")
    pt_code = codes[len(lab):].astype("int64")

    y = lab["churned_30d"].to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    commit = _sec(lab["_loaded_at"])
    t = _sec(points["as_of"])

    # global prior: mean churned_30d over all committed-before-t labels
    order = np.argsort(commit, kind="stable")
    ycum = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(y[order])])
    N = np.searchsorted(commit[order], t, side="left")
    S = ycum[N]
    prior = np.full(len(t), 0.05)
    has = N > 0
    prior[has] = S[has] / N[has]

    # district count/sum over committed-before-t labels
    key = lab_code * STRIDE + commit
    o2 = np.argsort(key, kind="stable")
    ycum2 = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(y[o2])])
    lo = np.searchsorted(key[o2], pt_code * STRIDE, side="left")
    hi = np.searchsorted(key[o2], pt_code * STRIDE + t, side="left")
    n = hi - lo
    s = ycum2[hi] - ycum2[lo]
    return (s + 20.0 * prior) / (n + 20.0)

    order = np.argsort(cids, kind="stable")
    sorted_cids = cids[order]
    # find boundaries
    change = np.concatenate([[True], sorted_cids[1:] != sorted_cids[:-1]])

    ends = np.concatenate([starts[1:], [len(sorted_cids)]])
    d = {}
    for s, e, c in zip(starts, ends, sorted_cids[starts]):
        idx = order[s:e]
        d[int(c)] = tuple(a[idx] for a in arrays)
    return d

import argparse
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from churn.extract import load_extract
from churn.impute import fill_app_minutes

EPOCH = pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01", tz="UTC")
STRIDE = 10 ** 10
DAY = 86400


def _sec(ts):
    return ((ts - EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)).to_numpy(dtype="int64")


def _bounds(cids):
    order = np.argsort(cids, kind="stable")
    sc = cids[order]
    change = np.concatenate(([True], sc[1:] != sc[:-1]))
    starts = np.flatnonzero(change)
    ends = np.concatenate((starts[1:], [sc.shape[0]]))
    return order, sc[starts], starts, ends


def _table_groups(df, cols):
    cids = df["customer_id"].to_numpy()
    order, c, s, e = _bounds(cids)
    d = {}
    for k in range(s.shape[0]):
        idx = order[s[k]:e[k]]
        d[int(c[k])] = [df[col].to_numpy()[idx] for col in cols]
    return d

"""Build the churn feature table: python -m churn.build_features --data <dir> --out <file.parquet>

For every row of scoring_points.csv, compute the value the live scoring service
(live/features.py) would have produced at that row's as_of, against the warehouse
as it stood at that moment: only rows and values committed before as_of count
(a row committed at or after as_of is not seen, an overwrite at or after as_of is
seen as it was before the overwrite).

Every feature of live/features.py whose live value the extract determines for every
row is kept.  days_since_last_login is left out: the customer's last login has no
history in the warehouse, so its value at an earlier as_of cannot be recovered.
"""
import argparse
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from churn.extract import load_extract
from churn.impute import fill_app_minutes

EPOCH = pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01", tz="UTC")
STRIDE = 10 ** 10  # customer_id * STRIDE + epoch seconds (seconds < 1e10 until 2286)
DAY = 86400


def _sec(ts):
    return ((ts - EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)).to_numpy(dtype="int64")


def _bounds(cids):
    """Return (order, group_ids, starts, ends) splitting an array by customer_id."""
    order = np.argsort(cids, kind="stable")
    sc = cids[order]
    change = np.concatenate(([True], sc[1:] != sc[:-1]))
    starts = np.flatnonzero(change)
    ends = np.concatenate((starts[1:], [sc.shape[0]]))
    return order, sc[starts], starts, ends


def _te_district(points, labels, customers):
    """Live te_district: (s + 20 p) / (n + 20) over all labels committed before t,
    where p is the global mean churned_30d (0.05 when none) and n, s are the count
    and sum over the customer's postcode district.  A label is committed at its
    _loaded_at, so it is seen at t iff _loaded_at < t."""
    dist = customers.set_index("customer_id")["postcode_district"]
    lab = labels.copy()
    lab["_d"] = lab["customer_id"].map(dist)
    lab = lab[lab["_d"].notna()]
    lab_d = lab["_d"].to_numpy()
    pt_d = points["customer_id"].map(dist).to_numpy()
    codes, _ = pd.factorize(np.concatenate([lab_d, pt_d]))
    lab_code = codes[: len(lab_d)].astype("int64")
    pt_code = codes[len(lab_d):].astype("int64")
    y = lab["churned_30d"].to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    commit = _sec(lab["_loaded_at"])
    t = _sec(points["as_of"])

    # global prior p: mean churned_30d over all labels with _loaded_at < t
    order = np.argsort(commit, kind="stable")
    ycum = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(y[order])])
    N = np.searchsorted(commit[order], t, side="left")
    S = ycum[N]
    prior = np.full(len(t), 0.05)
    has = N > 0
    prior[has] = S[has] / N[has]

    # district count/sum over labels with _loaded_at < t
    key = lab_code * STRIDE + commit
    o2 = np.argsort(key, kind="stable")
    ycum2 = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(y[o2])])
    lo = np.searchsorted(key[o2], pt_code * STRIDE, side="left")
    hi = np.searchsorted(key[o2], pt_code * STRIDE + t, side="left")
    n = hi - lo
    s = ycum2[hi] - ycum2[lo]
    return (s + 20.0 * prior) / (n + 20.0)


def build(data_dir):
    tb = load_extract(data_dir)
    points = tb["scoring_points"].reset_index(drop=True)
    n = len(points)
    cid = points["customer_id"].to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    t = _sec(points["as_of"])

    # ---- orders ---------------------------------------------------------------
    orders = tb["orders"]
    o_at = _sec(orders["ordered_at"])
    o_loaded = _sec(orders["_loaded_at"])
    o_amt = orders["amount_cents"].to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    oc = orders["customer_id"].to_numpy()
    oord, ocv, os, oe = _bounds(oc)
    o_grp = {}
    for k in range(os.shape[0]):
        idx = oord[os[k]:oe[k]]
        o_grp[int(ocv[k])] = (o_at[idx], o_loaded[idx], o_amt[idx])

    # ---- tickets --------------------------------------------------------------
    tickets = tb["tickets"]
    k_at = _sec(tickets["opened_at"])
    k_loaded = _sec(tickets["_loaded_at"])
    kc = tickets["customer_id"].to_numpy()
    kord, kcv, ks, ke = _bounds(kc)
    k_grp = {}
    for k in range(ks.shape[0]):
        idx = kord[ks[k]:ke[k]]
        k_grp[int(kcv[k])] = (k_at[idx], k_loaded[idx])

    # ---- status snapshots -----------------------------------------------------
    snaps = tb["status_snapshots"]
    s_date = _sec(snaps["snapshot_date"])
    s_loaded = _sec(snaps["_loaded_at"])
    s_status = snaps["status"].to_numpy()
    sc = snaps["customer_id"].to_numpy()
    sword, scv, ss, se = _bounds(sc)
    s_grp = {}
    for k in range(ss.shape[0]):
        idx = sword[ss[k]:se[k]]
        s_grp[int(scv[k])] = (s_date[idx], s_loaded[idx], s_status[idx])

    # ---- plan changes ---------------------------------------------------------
    pc = tb["plan_changes"]
    pc_changed = _sec(pc["changed_at"])
    pc_loaded = _sec(pc["_loaded_at"])
    pc_old = pc["old_plan"].to_numpy()
    pc_new = pc["new_plan"].to_numpy()
    pcid = pc["customer_id"].to_numpy()
    pord, pcv, ps, pe = _bounds(pcid)
    p_grp = {}
    p_base = {}
    for k in range(ps.shape[0]):
        idx = pord[ps[k]:pe[k]]
        ch = pc_changed[idx]
        c_id = int(pcv[k])
        p_grp[c_id] = (ch, pc_loaded[idx], pc_new[idx])
        p_base[c_id] = pc_old[idx][ch.argmin()]  # signup plan

    # ---- customers ------------------------------------------------------------
    ccid = customers_cid = tb["customers"]["customer_id"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    signup = dict(zip(ccid, _sec(tb["customers"]["signup_at"])))
    planmap = dict(zip(ccid, tb["customers"]["plan"].to_numpy()))

    # ---- per-customer computation ---------------------------------------------
    orders_7d = np.zeros(n, dtype="int64")
    orders_30d = np.zeros(n, dtype="int64")
    spend_30d = np.zeros(n, dtype="int64")
    tickets_30d = np.zeros(n, dtype="int64")
    dso = np.full(n, np.nan, dtype="float64")
    tenure = np.full(n, np.nan, dtype="float64")
    status = np.full(n, None, dtype=object)
    plan = np.full(n, None, dtype=object)

    pcids = points["customer_id"].to_numpy()
    po, pcv2, pps, ppe = _bounds(pcids)
    for k in range(pps.shape[0]):
        idx = po[pps[k]:ppe[k]]
        tt = t[idx]
        c = int(pcv2[k])

        if c in o_grp:
            oat, oload, oamt = o_grp[c]
            vis = oload[None, :] < tt[:, None]
            m7 = vis & (oat[None, :] >= tt[:, None] - 7 * DAY)
            m30 = vis & (oat[None, :] >= tt[:, None] - 30 * DAY)
            orders_7d[idx] = m7.sum(1)
            orders_30d[idx] = m30.sum(1)
            spend_30d[idx] = np.where(m30, oamt[None, :], 0).sum(1)
            last = np.where(vis, oat[None, :].astype("float64"), -1.0).max(1)
            dso[idx] = np.where(last < 0, np.nan, (tt - last) / DAY)

        if c in k_grp:
            kat, kload = k_grp[c]
            kvis = kload[None, :] < tt[:, None]
            tickets_30d[idx] = (kvis & (kat[None, :] >= tt[:, None] - 30 * DAY)).sum(1)

        tenure[idx] = (tt - signup[c]) / DAY

        if c in s_grp:
            sdate, sload, sstat = s_grp[c]
            sv = sload[None, :] < tt[:, None]
            sd = np.where(sv, sdate[None, :], -1)
            best = sd.argmax(1)
            has = sv.any(1)
            if has.any():
                status[idx[has]] = sstat[best[has]]

        base = p_base.get(c, planmap[c])
        pvals = np.full(idx.shape[0], base, dtype=object)
        if c in p_grp:
            pch, pload, pnew = p_grp[c]
            pv = pload[None, :] < tt[:, None]
            phas = pv.any(1)
            if phas.any():
                pd_ = np.where(pv, pch[None, :], -1)
                pvals[phas] = pnew[pd_.argmax(1)[phas]]
        plan[idx] = pvals

    app = fill_app_minutes(points).to_numpy()
    te = _te_district(points, tb["labels"], tb["customers"])

    return pd.DataFrame({
        "customer_id": cid,
        "as_of": points["as_of"],
        "orders_7d": orders_7d,
        "orders_30d": orders_30d,
        "spend_30d_cents": spend_30d,
        "tickets_30d": tickets_30d,
        "days_since_last_order": dso,
        "tenure_days": tenure,
        "status": status,
        "plan": plan,
        "app_minutes_7d": app,
        "te_district": te,
    })


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--data", required=True, help="folder with the extract CSVs")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output parquet file")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    feats = build(a.data)
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(a.out))
    if d:
        os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    feats.to_parquet(a.out, index=False)
    print(f"wrote {len(feats)} rows x {feats.shape[1]} columns to {a.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

steps.message:
Per-customer matrices are tiny (worst case 0.01 MB), so memory is a non-issue even for larger extracts. Now I'll apply two robustness hardenings: (1) add the SQL upper-bound `ordered_at < now` / `opened_at < now` to exactly mirror the live queries (redundant under the data invariants but exact), and (2) guard the customer lookups so a scoring customer absent from `customers` yields nulls (matching the live `FROM customers WHERE ...` NULL behavior) instead of crashing the run.

{
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "cat > /app/churn/build_features.py << 'PYEOF'
"""Build the churn feature table: python -m churn.build_features --data <dir> --out <file.parquet>

For every row of scoring_points.csv, compute the value the live scoring service
(live/features.py) would have produced at that row's as_of, against the warehouse
as it stood at that moment: only rows and values committed before as_of count
(a row committed at or after as_of is not seen, an overwrite at or after as_of is
seen as it was before the overwrite, whatever the date of the event the row records).

Every feature of live/features.py whose live value the extract determines for every
row is kept.  days_since_last_login is left out: the customer's last login has no
history in the warehouse, so its value at an earlier as_of cannot be recovered.
"""
import argparse
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from churn.extract import load_extract
from churn.impute import fill_app_minutes

EPOCH = pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01", tz="UTC")
STRIDE = 10 ** 10  # customer_id * STRIDE + epoch seconds (seconds < 1e10 until 2286)
DAY = 86400


def _sec(ts):
    return ((ts - EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)).to_numpy(dtype="int64")


def _bounds(cids):
    """Return (order, group_ids, starts, ends) splitting an array by customer_id."""
    order = np.argsort(cids, kind="stable")
    sc = cids[order]
    change = np.concatenate(([True], sc[1:] != sc[:-1]))
    starts = np.flatnonzero(change)
    ends = np.concatenate((starts[1:], [sc.shape[0]]))
    return order, sc[starts], starts, ends


def _groups(values, key_col):
    """{customer_id: values[rows of that customer]} from a frame keyed by key_col."""
    cids = values[key_col].to_numpy()
    order, cvals, starts, ends = _bounds(cids)
    out = {}
    for k in range(starts.shape[0]):
        out[int(cvals[k])] = order[starts[k]:ends[k]]
    return out


def _te_district(points, labels, customers):
    """Live te_district: (s + 20 p) / (n + 20) over all labels committed before t,
    where p is the global mean churned_30d (0.05 when none) and n, s are the count
    and sum over the customer's postcode district.  A label is committed at its
    _loaded_at, so it is seen at t iff _loaded_at < t."""
    dist = customers.set_index("customer_id")["postcode_district"]
    lab = labels.copy()
    lab["_d"] = lab["customer_id"].map(dist)
    lab = lab[lab["_d"].notna()]
    lab_d = lab["_d"].to_numpy()
    pt_d = points["customer_id"].map(dist).to_numpy()
    codes, _ = pd.factorize(np.concatenate([lab_d, pt_d]))
    lab_code = codes[: len(lab_d)].astype("int64")
    pt_code = codes[len(lab_d):].astype("int64")
    y = lab["churned_30d"].to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    commit = _sec(lab["_loaded_at"])
    t = _sec(points["as_of"])

    # global prior p: mean churned_30d over all labels with _loaded_at < t
    order = np.argsort(commit, kind="stable")
    ycum = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(y[order])])
    N = np.searchsorted(commit[order], t, side="left")
    S = ycum[N]
    prior = np.full(len(t), 0.05)
    has = N > 0
    prior[has] = S[has] / N[has]

    # district count/sum over labels with _loaded_at < t
    key = lab_code * STRIDE + commit
    o2 = np.argsort(key, kind="stable")
    ycum2 = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(y[o2])])
    lo = np.searchsorted(key[o2], pt_code * STRIDE, side="left")
    hi = np.searchsorted(key[o2], pt_code * STRIDE + t, side="left")
    n = hi - lo
    s = ycum2[hi] - ycum2[lo]
    return (s + 20.0 * prior) / (n + 20.0)


def build(data_dir):
    tb = load_extract(data_dir)
    points = tb["scoring_points"].reset_index(drop=True)
    n = len(points)
    cid = points["customer_id"].to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    t = _sec(points["as_of"])

    orders = tb["orders"]
    o_at = _sec(orders["ordered_at"])
    o_loaded = _sec(orders["_loaded_at"])
    o_amt = orders["amount_cents"].to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    o_idx = _groups(orders, "customer_id")

    tickets = tb["tickets"]
    k_at = _sec(tickets["opened_at"])
    k_loaded = _sec(tickets["_loaded_at"])
    k_idx = _groups(tickets, "customer_id")

    snaps = tb["status_snapshots"]
    s_date = _sec(snaps["snapshot_date"])
    s_loaded = _sec(snaps["_loaded_at"])
    s_status = snaps["status"].to_numpy()
    s_idx = _groups(snaps, "customer_id")

    pc = tb["plan_changes"]
    pc_changed = _sec(pc["changed_at"])
    pc_loaded = _sec(pc["_loaded_at"])
    pc_old = pc["old_plan"].to_numpy()
    pc_new = pc["new_plan"].to_numpy()
    pc_idx = _groups(pc, "customer_id")
    p_grp, p_base = {}, {}
    for c_id, r in pc_idx.items():
        ch = pc_changed[r]
        p_grp[c_id] = (ch, pc_loaded[r], pc_new[r])
        p_base[c_id] = pc_old[r][ch.argmin()]  # plan chosen at sign-up

    ccid = tb["customers"]["customer_id"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    signup = dict(zip(ccid, _sec(tb["customers"]["signup_at"])))
    planmap = dict(zip(ccid, tb["customers"]["plan"].to_numpy()))

    orders_7d = np.zeros(n, dtype="int64")
    orders_30d = np.zeros(n, dtype="int64")
    spend_30d = np.zeros(n, dtype="int64")
    tickets_30d = np.zeros(n, dtype="int64")
    dso = np.full(n, np.nan, dtype="float64")
    tenure = np.full(n, np.nan, dtype="float64")
    status = np.full(n, None, dtype=object)
    plan = np.full(n, None, dtype=object)

    po, pcv2, pps, ppe = _bounds(cid)
    for k in range(pps.shape[0]):
        idx = po[pps[k]:ppe[k]]
        tt = t[idx]
        c = int(pcv2[k])

        if c in o_idx:
            r = o_idx[c]
            oat, oload, oamt = o_at[r], o_loaded[r], o_amt[r]
            # visible at t iff committed before t and placed before t
            vis = (oload[None, :] < tt[:, None]) & (oat[None, :] < tt[:, None])
            m7 = vis & (oat[None, :] >= tt[:, None] - 7 * DAY)
            m30 = vis & (oat[None, :] >= tt[:, None] - 30 * DAY)
            orders_7d[idx] = m7.sum(1)
            orders_30d[idx] = m30.sum(1)
            spend_30d[idx] = np.where(m30, oamt[None, :], 0).sum(1)
            last = np.where(vis, oat[None, :].astype("float64"), -1.0).max(1)
            dso[idx] = np.where(last < 0, np.nan, (tt - last) / DAY)

        if c in k_idx:
            r = k_idx[c]
            kat, kload = k_at[r], k_loaded[r]
            kvis = (kload[None, :] < tt[:, None]) & (kat[None, :] < tt[:, None])
            tickets_30d[idx] = (kvis & (kat[None, :] >= tt[:, None] - 30 * DAY)).sum(1)

        supt = signup.get(c)
        if supt is not None:
            tenure[idx] = (tt - supt) / DAY

        if c in s_idx:
            r = s_idx[c]
            sdate, sload, sstat = s_date[r], s_loaded[r], s_status[r]
            # latest snapshot by snapshot_date among those committed before t
            sv = sload[None, :] < tt[:, None]
            sd = np.where(sv, sdate[None, :], -1)
            best = sd.argmax(1)
            has = sv.any(1)
            if has.any():
                status[idx[has]] = sstat[best[has]]

        base = p_base.get(c, planmap.get(c))
        if base is not None:
            pvals = np.full(idx.shape[0], base, dtype=object)
            if c in p_grp:
                pch, pload, pnew = p_grp[c]
                pv = pload[None, :] < tt[:, None]
                phas = pv.any(1)
                if phas.any():
                    pd_ = np.where(pv, pch[None, :], -1)
                    pvals[phas] = pnew[pd_.argmax(1)[phas]]
            plan[idx] = pvals

    app = fill_app_minutes(points).to_numpy()
    te = _te_district(points, tb["labels"], tb["customers"])

    return pd.DataFrame({
        "customer_id": cid,
        "as_of": points["as_of"],
        "orders_7d": orders_7d,
        "orders_30d": orders_30d,
        "spend_30d_cents": spend_30d,
        "tickets_30d": tickets_30d,
        "days_since_last_order": dso,
        "tenure_days": tenure,
        "status": status,
        "plan": plan,
        "app_minutes_7d": app,
        "te_district": te,
    })


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--data", required=True, help="folder with the extract CSVs")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output parquet file")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    feats = build(a.data)
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(a.out))
    if d:
        os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    feats.to_parquet(a.out, index=False)
    print(f"wrote {len(feats)} rows x {feats.shape[1]} columns to {a.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
PYEOF
echo written; wc -l /app/churn/build_features.py
",
      "duration": 0.5
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd /app && time OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 -m churn.build_features --data data --out /tmp/features.parquet
",
      "duration": 10.0
    }
  ]
}

cat > /app/churn/build_features.py << 'PYEOF'
"""Build the churn feature table: python -m churn.build_features --data <dir> --out <file.parquet>

For every row of scoring_points.csv, compute the value the live scoring service
(live/features.py) would have produced at that row's as_of, against the warehouse
as it stood at that moment: only rows and values committed before as_of count
(a row committed at or after as_of is not seen, an overwrite at or after as_of is
seen as it was before the overwrite, whatever the date of the event the row records).

Every feature of live/features.py whose live value the extract determines for every
row is kept.  days_since_last_login is left out: the customer's last login has no
history in the warehouse, so its value at an earlier as_of cannot be recovered.
"""
import argparse
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from churn.extract import load_extract
from churn.impute import fill_app_minutes

EPOCH = pd.Timestamp("1970-01-01", tz="UTC")
STRIDE = 10 ** 10  # customer_id * STRIDE + epoch seconds (seconds < 1e10 until 2286)
DAY = 86400


def _sec(ts):
    return ((ts - EPOCH) // pd.Timedelta(seconds=1)).to_numpy(dtype="int64")


def _bounds(cids):
    """Return (order, group_ids, starts, ends) splitting an array by customer_id."""
    order = np.argsort(cids, kind="stable")
    sc = cids[order]
    change = np.concatenate(([True], sc[1:] != sc[:-1]))
    starts = np.flatnonzero(change)
    ends = np.concatenate((starts[1:], [sc.shape[0]]))
    return order, sc[starts], starts, ends


def _groups(df, key_col):
    """{customer_id: index-array-of-that-customer's rows} for a frame's rows."""
    cids = df[key_col].to_numpy()
    order, cvals, starts, ends = _bounds(cids)
    return {int(cvals[k]): order[starts[k]:ends[k]] for k in range(starts.shape[0])}


def _te_district(points, labels, customers):
    """Live te_district: (s + 20 p) / (n + 20) over all labels committed before t,
    where p is the global mean churned_30d (0.05 when none) and n, s are the count
    and sum over the customer's postcode district.  A label is committed at its
    _loaded_at, so it is seen at t iff _loaded_at < t."""
    dist = customers.set_index("customer_id")["postcode_district"]
    lab = labels.copy()
    lab["_d"] = lab["customer_id"].map(dist)
    lab = lab[lab["_d"].notna()]
    lab_d = lab["_d"].to_numpy()
    pt_d = points["customer_id"].map(dist).to_numpy()
    codes, _ = pd.factorize(np.concatenate([lab_d, pt_d]))
    lab_code = codes[: len(lab_d)].astype("int64")
    pt_code = codes[len(lab_d):].astype("int64")
    y = lab["churned_30d"].to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    commit = _sec(lab["_loaded_at"])
    t = _sec(points["as_of"])

    # global prior p: mean churned_30d over all labels with _loaded_at < t
    order = np.argsort(commit, kind="stable")
    ycum = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(y[order])])
    N = np.searchsorted(commit[order], t, side="left")
    S = ycum[N]
    prior = np.full(len(t), 0.05)
    has = N > 0
    prior[has] = S[has] / N[has]

    # district count/sum over labels with _loaded_at < t
    key = lab_code * STRIDE + commit
    o2 = np.argsort(key, kind="stable")
    ycum2 = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(y[o2])])
    lo = np.searchsorted(key[o2], pt_code * STRIDE, side="left")
    hi = np.searchsorted(key[o2], pt_code * STRIDE + t, side="left")
    n = hi - lo
    s = ycum2[hi] - ycum2[lo]
    return (s + 20.0 * prior) / (n + 20.0)


def build(data_dir):
    tb = load_extract(data_dir)
    points = tb["scoring_points"].reset_index(drop=True)
    n = len(points)
    cid = points["customer_id"].to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    t = _sec(points["as_of"])

    orders = tb["orders"]
    o_at = _sec(orders["ordered_at"])
    o_loaded = _sec(orders["_loaded_at"])
    o_amt = orders["amount_cents"].to_numpy(dtype="int64")
    o_grp = _groups(orders, "customer_id")

    tickets = tb["tickets"]
    k_at = _sec(tickets["opened_at"])
    k_loaded = _sec(tickets["_loaded_at"])
    k_grp = _groups(tickets, "customer_id")

    snaps = tb["status_snapshots"]
    s_date = _sec(snaps["snapshot_date"])
    s_loaded = _sec(snaps["_loaded_at"])
    s_status = snaps["status"].to_numpy()
    s_grp = _groups(snaps, "customer_id")

    pc = tb["plan_changes"]
    pc_changed = _sec(pc["changed_at"])
    pc_loaded = _sec(pc["_loaded_at"])
    pc_old = pc["old_plan"].to_numpy()
    pc_new = pc["new_plan"].to_numpy()
    pc_rows = _groups(pc, "customer_id")
    p_grp, p_base = {}, {}
    for c_id, r in pc_rows.items():
        ch = pc_changed[r]
        p_grp[c_id] = (ch, pc_loaded[r], pc_new[r])
        p_base[c_id] = pc_old[r][ch.argmin()]  # plan chosen at sign-up

    ccid = tb["customers"]["customer_id"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    signup = dict(zip(ccid, _sec(tb["customers"]["signup_at"])))
    planmap = dict(zip(ccid, tb["customers"]["plan"].to_numpy()))

    orders_7d = np.zeros(n, dtype="int64")
    orders_30d = np.zeros(n, dtype="int64")
    spend_30d = np.zeros(n, dtype="int64")
    tickets_30d = np.zeros(n, dtype="int64")
    dso = np.full(n, np.nan, dtype="float64")
    tenure = np.full(n, np.nan, dtype="float64")
    status = np.full(n, None, dtype=object)
    plan = np.full(n, None, dtype=object)

    po, pcv2, pps, ppe = _bounds(cid)
    for k in range(pps.shape[0]):
        idx = po[pps[k]:ppe[k]]
        tt = t[idx]
        c = int(pcv2[k])

        if c in o_grp:
            r = o_grp[c]
            oat, oload, oamt = o_at[r], o_loaded[r], o_amt[r]
            vis = (oload[None, :] < tt[:, None]) & (oat[None, :] < tt[:, None])
            m7 = vis & (oat[None, :] >= tt[:, None] - 7 * DAY)
            m30 = vis & (oat[None, :] >= tt[:, None] - 30 * DAY)
            orders_7d[idx] = m7.sum(1)
            orders_30d[idx] = m30.sum(1)
            spend_30d[idx] = np.where(m30, oamt[None, :], 0).sum(1)
            last = np.where(vis, oat[None, :].astype("float64"), -1.0).max(1)
            dso[idx] = np.where(last < 0, np.nan, (tt - last) / DAY)

        if c in k_grp:
            r = k_grp[c]
            kat, kload = k_at[r], k_loaded[r]
            kvis = (kload[None, :] < tt[:, None]) & (kat[None, :] < tt[:, None])
            tickets_30d[idx] = (kvis & (kat[None, :] >= tt[:, None] - 30 * DAY)).sum(1)

        supt = signup.get(c)
        if supt is not None:
            tenure[idx] = (tt - supt) / DAY

        if c in s_grp:
            r = s_grp[c]
            sdate, sload, sstat = s_date[r], s_loaded[r], s_status[r]
            sv = sload[None, :] < tt[:, None]
            sd = np.where(sv, sdate[None, :], -1)
            best = sd.argmax(1)
            has = sv.any(1)
            if has.any():
                status[idx[has]] = sstat[best[has]]

        base = p_base.get(c, planmap.get(c))
        if base is not None:
            pvals = np.full(idx.shape[0], base, dtype=object)
            if c in p_grp:
                pch, pload, pnew = p_grp[c]
                pv = pload[None, :] < tt[:, None]
                phas = pv.any(1)
                if phas.any():
                    pd_ = np.where(pv, pch[None, :], -1)
                    pvals[phas] = pnew[pd_.argmax(1)[phas]]
            plan[idx] = pvals

    app = fill_app_minutes(points).to_numpy()
    te = _te_district(points, tb["labels"], tb["customers"])

    return pd.DataFrame({
        "customer_id": cid,
        "as_of": points["as_of"],
        "orders_7d": orders_7d,
        "orders_30d": orders_30d,
        "spend_30d_cents": spend_30d,
        "tickets_30d": tickets_30d,
        "days_since_last_order": dso,
        "tenure_days": tenure,
        "status": status,
        "plan": plan,
        "app_minutes_7d": app,
        "te_district": te,
    })


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--data", required=True, help="folder with the extract CSVs")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output parquet file")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    feats = build(a.data)
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(a.out))
    if d:
        os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    feats.to_parquet(a.out, index=False)
    print(f"wrote {len(feats)} rows x {feats.shape[1]} columns to {a.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
